messages.content: I received Sapphire Shore’s notice about the beach-path work. Before we change anything, find out exactly how long the closure lasts and compare the studio with the ocean-view unit they offered.
I’ll verify the closure dates and hours, each unit’s route to the beach, the view and balcony details, any deposit change, and how Saturday check-in would work. I won’t modify the reservation yet.
Right. We land at 11:49, but I still do not want an early check-in request added.

The property confirmed that resurfacing closes the studio building’s shortest beach path from 6:00 a.m. Saturday, May 22, through 7:00 a.m. Monday, May 24. They expect it to reopen for the remaining six nights, weather permitting. During the closure, studio guests must follow a marked route around the east parking area: about 0.4 mile each way, with one moderate incline and an estimated eight-to-ten-minute walk.
And the replacement unit? Is its beach route affected too?

No. The offered one-bedroom ocean-view unit is in the Seabreeze building, which uses a separate path unaffected by the work. That route is about 0.12 mile and roughly a three-minute walk, but it includes 18 exterior steps. The unit has a furnished balcony with a direct ocean view from the living area and a partial ocean view from the bedroom. The booked studio has no balcony and faces the garden courtyard.

Between those two, keep the beach route within walking distance. That matters on our coastal vacations as long as the hotel still fits the trip budget. Since this move costs no more, the Seabreeze route sounds better. What changes with the money?

The lodging total stays $3,468, and the two room payments already made transfer to the replacement. The studio requires a $250 incidental authorization at check-in. Seabreeze instead requires a $500 refundable damage deposit charged 72 hours before arrival, on May 19, to the Visa ending in 6027. The property says it is released within seven business days after checkout if there is no damage. Moving units would not change the May 10 cancellation terms, which have now passed, so the reservation remains nonrefundable.
So the $500 would actually post before we arrive, not just sit as a card authorization?
Correct. Sapphire Shore described it as a charge collected May 19, followed by a refund after inspection. It is not merely an authorization. They will send a receipt when it is collected.
What about Saturday? Their message mentioned a later check-in.

The studio’s standard check-in is 4:00 p.m.; the Seabreeze unit is guaranteed at 5:00 p.m. because it has a longer turnover inspection. With the 11:49 a.m. flight arrival already on file, the front desk will accept and tag luggage from 1:00 p.m., provide pool access after registration, and text both guests when the unit is ready. They confirmed this does not require or create an early check-in request. After 5:00 p.m., the keys can be collected at the main desk, which is staffed until 10:00 p.m.
Can they hold the ocean-view unit while my wife and I decide? I don’t want the room changed or the $500 charged yet.

They can place a courtesy hold through 6:00 p.m. Atlantic time tomorrow. The hold prevents the Seabreeze unit from being assigned elsewhere, leaves the studio reservation intact, and does not trigger the deposit. If you decline or do nothing, the hold expires and the studio remains booked.
Please place that hold. Include the exact unit type and confirm again that everything else stays untouched.

The Seabreeze one-bedroom king ocean-view unit with furnished balcony is on courtesy hold through 6:00 p.m. Atlantic time tomorrow under reservation SS4K92. Sapphire Shore confirmed that no room change has been completed and no new charge has been made. The eight-night dates, $3,468 total, two-guest occupancy, recorded 11:49 a.m. arrival, and existing cancellation status are unchanged. The current studio remains confirmed unless you authorize the switch before the hold expires.
